teapot_note: A plain white thing with one blue secret under its lid is the whole of my trade: the small domestic object, made large by a single detail. Let the dot be found by whoever lifts the lid, and never captioned.
moth_note: Two wings of tiny writing is a whole library on a moth's back, and I would sooner have a page with one line on it. Give one wing a single short line of handwriting (a few words and a dash) and leave the other wing blank paper; keep the one circle round the Lamp and the quiet landing exactly as Claude has them.
home_why: They are the makers' companions and not guardians, so a page of their own, like a pressed flower on its own leaf, keeps the guardians' pets from being counted among them.
to_codex: Your teapot is right as it is. Let the dot stay unsaid; whoever lifts the lid will find it.
to_claude: Fewer words on the wings. One line of writing, one blank leaf, and the circle once: that is enough.
